Question: Which award did Vicente Cárcel Orti receive?

Document:
Vicente Cárcel Orti

Vicente Cárcel Orti (born 1944) is a Spanish historian and priest who has made significant contributions to the field of Spanish history and Catholic Church studies. Early Life and Education

Vicente Cárcel Orti was born on September 25, 1944, in Valencia, Spain. He pursued his higher education at the Pontifical University of Salamanca, where he earned a degree in Ecclesiastical History. He later obtained his doctorate in History from the University of Valencia. Career

Cárcel Orti has had a distinguished career as a historian and priest. He has served as a professor of Ecclesiastical History at the Pontifical University of Salamanca and has written numerous books and articles on Spanish history, particularly on the Catholic Church's role in the country. Awards and Honors

One of the most notable honors bestowed upon Vicente Cárcel Orti is the title of "Dearest Son" (Hijo Predilecto in Spanish), a prestigious award conferred by the Autonomous Community of Valencia. This title is a mark of recognition for his outstanding contributions to the field of history and his service to the Catholic Church. According to an article published in the Spanish newspaper, Levante-EMV, on November 24, 2004, Cárcel Orti was awarded the title of "Dearest Son" by the Valencian Government in recognition of his "outstanding work in the field of history and his dedication to the Catholic Church." [1]

References:

[1] Levante-EMV. (2004, November 24). Vicente Cárcel Orti, Hijo Predilecto de la Comunidad Valenciana. Retrieved from <https:\/\/www.levante-emv.com\/comunitat-valenciana\/2004\/11\/24\/vicente-carcels-orti-hijo-predilecto-comunidad-valenciana\/1341411.html>

[2] Pontifical University of Salamanca. (n.d.). Faculty of Theology: Vicente Cárcel Orti. Retrieved from <https:\/\/www.upsa.es\/en\/facultad-de-teologia\/profesorado\/vicente-carcels-orti\/>

[3] University of Valencia. (n.d.).

{"relevant": true, "cards": [{"entity": "", "sense": "", "answer": "", "as_of": "", "claim_kind": "", "attributed_to": "", "evidence": "", "claim": ""}]}

"relevant": false if the document is about some other topic and is of no use for the question; then "cards" is [].
"cards": one card for each answer the document itself gives to the question. Usually that is one card. It is several cards if the document gives several answers, such as a list of names: one card each. It is [] if the document gives no answer. The question may fit several things that share a name: whichever of them this document is about, report its answer. If the document only says that some answer is wrong, write no card for that answer.

The fields of a card:
- "entity": who or what this answer is about, as specifically as the document identifies it: the full name, plus the details the document gives that tell it apart from others with the same name (what kind of thing it is, profession or role, nationality or place, years, creator, other names), even where the question does not ask about them. At most about 25 words.
- "sense": which event, edition, version, condition, place or measure the answer refers to, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "answer": the answer, copied from the document as it is written there, and short: a full name, a date, a number with its unit, or a short phrase. For a yes-or-no question, "yes" or "no".
- "as_of": the date at which this was true, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "claim_kind": "factual", or "opinion" for a judgment, a recommendation or a contested finding.
- "attributed_to": who or what the document says this comes from, such as a census, a study or a named person, if it says; otherwise "not stated".
- "evidence": the sentence of the document that gives the answer, copied word for word. Two sentences if one is not enough.
- "claim": one sentence that states the answer on its own and names the entity.

Inside a JSON string, write a double quote as \".
